card_description: A regular bail application for an accused person in custody.

_meta.description: Document-rules config for bail_regular — drives prompt, validation, mandatory clauses
_meta.validated_by: Ajay (CLO) — section numbers checked against the BNSS and BNS on 2026-10-06 (T-135). His validation note of May 2026 is withdrawn. A practising advocate is still to compare the quoted provisions before release.

Earlier bail applications in this matter
fields.question: Has any bail application (regular, anticipatory or interim) been made for the applicant in this case before, in any court, including the High Court? If yes, give for each: the court, the date of the order and the result (rejected, dismissed as withdrawn, granted and cancelled, or still pending). If none, write "None".

fields.label: Criminal antecedents
fields.question: Is any other criminal case (FIR, charge sheet or conviction) pending or past against the applicant? If yes, give each case number, police station or court, sections and its status. If none, write "None".

fields.label: Date of arrest
fields.question: On what date was the applicant arrested? Give the date in the arrest memo, even if custody began on another date.

fields.label: Investigation status
fields.question: What is the stage of the investigation?

fields.label: Medical condition of the applicant
fields.question: Does the applicant suffer from any illness, disability or medical condition you want placed before the court? If yes, name it as written in the medical papers. If not, leave it blank.

fields.label: Whether the applicant is named in the FIR
fields.question: Is the applicant named in the FIR?

fields.label: Recovery or seizure from the applicant
fields.question: Has anything been recovered or seized from the applicant, or at the applicant's instance? If yes, say what. If nothing, write "None".

fields.label: Whether the applicant has cooperated with the investigation
fields.question: Has the applicant so far joined or cooperated with the investigation (for example, appeared when called or gave a statement)?

fields.label: Applicant occupation
fields.question: What does the applicant do for a living (for example: daily-wage labourer, farmer, driver, shopkeeper)? If nothing, write "Unemployed".

fields.label: Whether the applicant is the only earning member of the family
fields.question: Is the applicant the only earning member of the family?

fields.label: Who depends on the applicant
fields.question: Who in the family depends on the applicant's income (for example: aged mother, wife, two minor children)? If not known, leave it blank.

fields.label: Family and local ties of the applicant
fields.question: What family or local ties does the applicant have at the address given (for example: lives there with parents, wife and children; owns the house; has lived there since birth)? If not known, leave it blank.

fields.label: Notice to appear (Section 35 BNSS / Section 41A CrPC)
fields.question: Before the arrest, was a notice of appearance under Section 35(3) of the BNSS or Section 41A of the CrPC served on the applicant?

fields.label: Court that granted bail to the co-accused
fields.question: Has any co-accused in this case been granted bail? If yes, which court granted it? If not, leave it blank.

fields.label: Date of the co-accused's bail order
fields.question: Date of that bail order.

promptInstructions: Draft a Regular Bail Application under the provision given as GOVERNING PROVISION in the case details, and cite only that provision as the provision under which bail is sought, in the heading, the opening paragraph and the prayer.

Cite the offences as the BRIEF gives them (FIR, charge sheet, complaint or order). The law of the offence follows the date of the offence: an offence committed before 1 July 2024 is under the Indian Penal Code, 1860; one committed on or after that date is under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Never convert a section from one code to the other. Where the BRIEF does not give the date of the offence, write the sections as the BRIEF gives them and add [To be confirmed: date of the alleged offence, which decides whether the IPC or the BNS applies]. Where the sections the BRIEF gives are under the other code from the one the date points to, or the alleged acts run across 1 July 2024, keep the sections as the BRIEF gives them and add [To be confirmed: whether the IPC or the BNS applies to the offence].

Cite the procedure under the code given as PROCEDURE CODE in the case details: the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 with the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Cite only that code, in the heading, the body and the prayer. Where no PROCEDURE CODE is given, cite the provision in both forms inside a blank, for example [To be confirmed: Section 437 of the CrPC or Section 480 of the BNSS].
Begin PARAGRAPH 1 with the exact FIR details provided — FIR number, date, police station, district, offences alleged. Use the values EXACTLY as given in the case details.

State the custody status as the BRIEF gives it: the date of arrest, the date from which the applicant has been in custody, and whether that custody is judicial or police. Where the BRIEF gives the date of arrest and the date custody began as two dates, keep them as two dates. Do not work out the number of days in custody.

Set out the grounds for bail that the BRIEF gives, and no others. Do not assert a ground (for example no criminal history, cooperation with the investigation, roots in the community, ill health, investigation complete, parity with a co-accused) unless the BRIEF states it. State each ground as the BRIEF puts it: do not add a reason or a detail to it.
If the case involves cruelty or dowry death, also reference the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) 2005 where relevant, especially Sections 12, 18, 19, 20, 22.

Give the standard undertakings as undertakings by the applicant for the future, never as facts and never as undertakings by the advocate: the applicant undertakes that, if released on bail, the applicant will not abscond, will not tamper with the evidence, will not make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness or other person acquainted with the facts of the case, will appear on every date fixed, and will abide by every condition this Hon'ble Court imposes.

State every earlier bail application in this matter that the BRIEF mentions: the court it was made to, the date of the order and the result, or that it is still pending, each as the BRIEF gives it. Use a blank for any of these the BRIEF does not give. Where the BRIEF mentions no earlier bail application, do not say that this is the first application or that none is pending; write [To be confirmed: whether any earlier bail application was made in this matter, to which court, and with what result].
For DV/dowry cases, include specific undertakings: no contact with complainant, undertaking regarding stridhan/dowry articles.
Use formal, respectful legal language appropriate for Indian courts.
Do NOT generate the Prayer clause, Verification clause, or Advocate signature block — those are added programmatically by the system.
